correctness.rationale: Every finite union-convex family has a unique maximum U and becomes a nonempty upset of P(U); conversely every nonempty upset is a weak ideal with maximum U. This proves the exact binomial-Dedekind transform and E_N=W_N-M_N. The classical asymptotic log2 M_n=(1+o(1))*binom(n,floor(n/2)) implies both the tail estimate R_N<=2^N M_(N-2)=o(N M_(N-1)) and the sharp logarithmic exponent. Direct exhaustive independent closure and upset tests checked every family up to four valuations. The finite tests do not certify infinity or independently establish exact M8.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete finite-vocabulary semantic invariant for recently translated bilateral state logic, not a cherry-picked sample. The quantified limit shows that non-upward meanings are exponentially rare in the central-binomial exponent despite nonmonotonic expressiveness, and the exceptional distributions concentrate on a one-valuation missing maximum. This probabilistic/structural contrast matters to counting semantic behavior, typical-case reasoning, and benchmark selection; no downstream theorem beyond this exact spectrum is required. The result is only about uniform support-equivalence classes, not formula frequency.
